title: Bonus Stage
text: “As for that side of things, it actually came out years later that she’d been secretly learning from Ark-sensei on the side too, you know. So it made sense that they got along.”
“Hold on a moment, I say. You’re telling me that despite Ark being so terrifyingly beloved, there was already a spouse in the picture?”

“Ah, so you finally noticed. Yeah. See, the reason it’s terrifying is… spirit-types, when they die, the spirit part separates from the body and turns into a spirit, right? Well, the soul and will attached to the body are… frankly, pretty messed up. This is the kind of story that’ll make your face go pale—still want to hear it?”
“Y-yikes…”
That was an ominous setup, I say. Something being “messed up” sounded frightening indeed.

“Well, to soften it a bit—or rather, to put it more accurately—in some worlds, there are cases where a hero becomes a sacrifice, sealing some unspeakably vile Demon Lord or concept of ruin into their own body at the cost of their life. When that thing revives, it takes control of the hero’s body, and if you destroy that body, its true form emerges to try and drag the world into ruin.”
“Hm? Now that you mention it, didn’t Ark say something once, laughing, about having been a Demon Lord too?”

“Yep. By that point he wasn’t doing anything evil anymore, living peacefully, basically watching over the second generation as they became independent… and yet somehow, someone managed to defile poor innocent Ark-sensei like that. And apparently this was the second time it happened. The first time, the Spirit of demonkind willingly handed over her body and possessed him, and the two ended up blending together—he lost his memories, got weakened, and she lingered inside his body for a while afterward… persistent, huh?”

In my mind, I pictured gentle Father, smiling warmly as he raised young Big Sister and Tiger Girl like a parent. Then, in my imagination, once the two of them grew up, unable to hold back any longer, they lunged at Father—and the screen cut to black, I say.
“I think you should stop imagining that, because they’d actually kill you for it.”
“Don’t read my thoughts, I say!”

“Well, the general shape of it isn’t too far off, but it’s something else entirely. Anyway, the point is, the second generation offered up their body and soul, and carved something into Ark-sensei as a result. Thanks to that, I ended up being taught by him too—back then, being able to see spirits was thanks to that very thing.”
So this was part of Ark’s past, I say. So he’d been sealed—or rather, trapped—inside the body of some yandere like that?
“What a terrifying tale, I say.”

“It was something done right before death, from an irresistible curse that had been placed on me too. Rather than just dying outright, it was a two-birds-one-stone deal—conveying feelings while also doing this. And after that, Ark-sensei came to clearly understand the whole spirit-type problem. He didn’t have as much power back then either.”
So that’s the kind of past Ark carries with him.
“Just like Father, it seems Ark is also the receiving type, I say.”
“Haha…”
The spear spirit gave a dry laugh, I say.
“Well, regardless, this time you took a different course of action than usual, and for the next loop, as long as you remember something similar, I’d like you to try exploring other approaches too…”
“Even without you saying so, I’ll give it some thought, I say. Let’s see… what if I cast Fairy Morph on someone right from the start, I say?”
“That part, at least, seems like it could be changed fairly easily.”

Oh? Seems the spear spirit approved too, I say. But… hmm, perhaps consulting Father first would be the wiser move, I say. The trouble is, if I go asking him with too much familiarity right off the bat, he tends to keep his distance, I say. Which reminded me—when I take on the form of an usaunny, Father smiles at me so gently, I say. That’s it, I say. If the chance arises, I’ll go ask Father on the night of the second day. Whether he wants some stimulation or not. Depending on his answer, I’ll proceed accordingly, I say. The plan was coming together nicely.

“Well, one more thing… no matter how much of a grudge you’re holding, doing that sort of thing to Takt, a fellow reincarnator, isn’t exactly great, you know? Not good for your karma, or your soul, either.”

“That’s one thing I can’t back down on, I say! That bastard desecrated Filolial-sama, so I refuse to let him die easy, I say! And I haven’t forgotten about what happened to Fleon-chan either, so the Crimson Swine shares equal guilt, I say!”
“Wow… well, I guess in your case this particular matter isn’t all that serious anyway.”
“It is serious, I say!”
“That’s not what I meant… ah, never mind.”
Just then, my body began to float upward, I say.
“Alright, it’s about time for the next loop.”
“Already, I say?”

I felt like there were still a few more things I wanted to point out to the spear spirit, I say. Just as I thought that, my body kept drifting higher and higher… and just as I was about to slip into the loop, my consciousness grew distant—
Suddenly, a slashing sound rang out above me, like something had been cut clean through, I say. With a whoosh, gravity seemed to reassert itself all at once, and I found myself falling, I say.
“Guh!”
Just when I thought I was about to be flung into a new loop, I plummeted rapidly and slammed into the ground instead.
“Oh my… I was going to set it to random and send you off, but I never expected you’d draw that one.”
“W-why did that happen, I say?”

“Well, you see, Ark-sensei set it up so you wouldn’t get hurt… you got lucky. If it had gone through as planned, you’d have ended up in a pretty rough loop for you. Specifically, one involving your greatest fear—Filo-chan’s—”
“HIIIIIYAAAAA!?”
Just from that much, I knew exactly where that loop would have led. So Ark had set up something specifically to prevent that from happening!?

“There are other loops too—ones where you drove him to the absolute edge, or loops that would’ve been bad for you or for him—those got the same treatment and weren’t constructed, so those branches don’t exist. So, I could just redo the draw, but… no… wait, I’ve got it.”
The spear spirit seemed to mull something over, then lit up as if struck by inspiration.

“Yeah. If I use that… heh, this could get interesting. There are traces of someone having rigged something similar in your world too, so, yeah. It’s interesting, and the timing’s just right, so let’s try it. A little extra latitude like this should be fine.”
“Muttering to yourself like that, I can’t follow along at all, I say.”

“Well, of course, since I’m trying to surprise you. Let’s see… while we’re at it, maybe I should explain why hero summoning has to be initiated from the human side. Originally, it was optional—I could call whenever I liked, at my own timing.”
Ah, I see—if the spirit had a will of her own, then being able to summon freely would surely be better for whoever got summoned too, I say. Strange places… Father suffered because of that too, I say.

“But each time the worlds fuse together, that sort of thing becomes harder to do. Things that were originally separate end up stuck together, after all. It’s like the specifications stop matching up properly. So it becomes more a matter of calling through whatever opening the human-side summoning creates, whenever the chance arises.”
“I see, I say.”

So that’s why hero summonings exist, I say. Which means the very first Sacred Weapon heroes could be called and placed by the spirits whenever needed, I say. Hmm… so not even being able to summon freely is a hassle for spirits too, I say. Hm? Well, this seemed like a good opportunity to ask something.
“Something just occurred to me from that last topic, I say.”
“What?”
“It’s something I’d really rather ask the shield spirit directly, I say.”
“Ah, well, you’re probably never going to meet her, so you’d best ask me instead.”
“Then I will, I say. Why does Father have so little attack power, I say?”
I’d always assumed it was just the build the shield spirit had chosen, but I figured I’d confirm it properly, I say.
“Ah, that? Well, it’s not the shield spirit’s fault. In fact, there have been heroes chosen by the shield spirit in the past who had plenty of offensive capability.”
What—so past Shield Heroes other than Father actually could attack, I say?
“It’s simply his nature. He originally belongs to the realm of Reverie, you see.”
“Infinity, I say? Well, Father certainly does possess infinite mercy.”
“Not that kind of ‘mugen’—I mean ‘muken,’ dream and illusion, reverie. There’s no way Ark-sensei, of all people, would be fond of infinity.”
Reverie? I wondered if the spear spirit even realized he was using technical jargon. I hadn’t the faintest idea what he meant, I say.

“Even in the demon-woman’s prophecy, there was no mention of this—but even if I’d chosen him instead of you, his attack power would still be considerably low. Do you remember? Long ago, when the Shield’s Sacred Weapon was temporarily stolen from him, and the staff spirit lent her power instead? Even then, she was fighting using the borrowed attack power of the original wielder. Well, since the opponent was a cheater, there was apparently some bonus attack power added on top.”

So it seemed that merely wielding a weapon with a spirit dwelling in it applied some kind of negative correction to attack power, I say. From the sound of it, this must be about the time Father borrowed a weapon from Trash, I say. Apparently he teamed up with Tiger Guy and put Takt through absolute hell. Truly worthy of Father, I say. And it seemed that with the Shield’s Sacred Weapon, Father simply couldn’t draw out any attack power from it, no matter what.
“Could you not simply dwell in Father’s hand yourself, I say?”

“You know full well what kind of spirit I am, right? The shield can function somewhat as auxiliary equipment too, sure. But—in that case, it would have to go through you, and for that loop, there’s the matter of connecting your memories and stats and all that. Ah, and if we swapped things around, you’d end up lost and adrift, with no good outcome waiting for you either way. I don’t think you could handle overcoming his situation, you know?”

The spear spirit seemed to have run the numbers and concluded it simply wasn’t feasible. Gah… I say. Father’s circumstances back then must have been that brutal. Now that I thought about it, back in those days, I hadn’t possessed anywhere near Father’s level of survival skill, I say.

“Anyway, that’s enough on that topic for now… The world you’re about to head into next is, I suppose you could call it a bonus stage of sorts. Things are going to turn out even more different than before.”
“A bonus stage, I say?”

“Well, whether it’s a bonus stage for you specifically, I couldn’t say. But, just like you said, there are places you can only reach because everyone, each and every one, has repeated countless regrets to get there. This might be the reverse of that.”
And with that, my body gently began to float upward once more.
“Well then, Motoyasu Kitamura—let’s see what kind of actions you take in the next world.”
The spear spirit sounded almost like he was testing me, I say.
“Knowing you, I’m sure the next world will turn out fine. Just follow whatever your heart commands. Doing your best for someone else—that’s who you are, isn’t it?”
“Who said you could go deciding that on your own, I say!”
“Just one piece of advice, though. No matter how much you try to change things, once a hero is summoned next, that choice is fixed. No one else will be called in their place. Keep that in mind.”
I’ll turn him into a cart axle again for sure this time, I say! And so, once more, I found myself looping again.
That concludes the Slave Trader Arc. Starting next, we move into the Reverie Arc… the Siltvelt Arc, Another version.
